public.label: 01 / PUBLIC POLICY TRANSITION
public.title: Preparing an economy for life beyond trade preferences.
public.desc: LDC graduation alters preference margins, financing conditions and the terms of competition. Research helps sequence a transition rather than react to each shock separately.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Fragmented intelligence on preferences and access
Gaps in productive capacity and export diversification
Financing and reform priorities disconnected

private.label: 01 / EXPORTER MARKET-ACCESS STRATEGY
private.title: What does the loss of a tariff preference mean for an exporter?
private.desc: When preferential access changes, the immediate impact depends on buyers, margins, country of origin, product mix and substitution possibilities—not a headline tariff alone.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.problemTitle: A buyer strategy built on one advantage.
problems: Price competitiveness tied to preferences
Country and buyer concentration poorly mapped
Limited analysis of switching and certification costs
outputs: Buyer- and product-level tariff exposure map

public.label: 02 / TRADE POLICY AND TARIFF SHOCKS
public.title: Turning tariff uncertainty into a policy response.
public.desc: A tariff announcement is not an economy-wide outcome. Its transmission depends on sector composition, demand elasticity, exchange rates, value chains and partner responses.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
public.problemTitle: A single shock. Many competing claims.
problems: Tariff headlines mistaken for predicted export losses
Product exposure and elasticities not reconciled
Response options lack distributional review

private.label: 02 / EXPORT PRICE AND DEMAND RISK
private.title: Protecting margins when foreign market conditions turn.
private.desc: An exporting firm may face higher buyer prices, weaker orders and fluctuating exchange rates at the same time. A useful strategy separates price, volume, margin and local-currency cash flow.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: FX revenue confused with real profitability
Buyer price sensitivity untested
Order concentration and input exposure hidden
private.outputTitle: A conditional export and pricing strategy.

public.label: 03 / TRADE IN SERVICES
public.title: Making invisible trade barriers visible.
public.desc: Services exports may face licensing, payment, data-flow, skills and recognition barriers that do not appear as conventional border tariffs. Good diagnostics identify which constraints can actually change.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Fragmented information on cross-border services
Regulatory and payments constraints unmapped
Weak classification and firm-level evidence
outputs: Tradable service and market opportunity map
Measurable policy indicators and dialogue plan

private.label: 03 / DIGITAL SERVICES EXPORTS
private.title: Choosing where a digital exporter should compete.
private.desc: Software and professional-service exporters compete across skills, contracts, trust, payments and buyer discovery. Market entry needs evidence about reachable demand and the true cost of delivery.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Markets ranked using size, not accessible demand
Client acquisition cost and compliance overlooked
Cross-border billing and delivery risk uncertain

public.label: 04 / PRODUCTIVE CAPACITY & GREEN TRADE
public.title: Finding the productive constraints behind slow diversification.
public.desc: Trade performance depends on far more than market access. Energy, transport, institutions, finance and firm capabilities shape the ability to move into higher-value exports.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Sector targets detached from production bottlenecks
Infrastructure and skills constraints fragmented
Green transition investment priorities unclear

private.label: 04 / INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTIVITY
private.title: Testing whether technology adoption actually pays.
private.desc: Factory-level energy efficiency decisions often stall when firms cannot verify savings, financing payback or operational risk. Randomised evidence and firm-level data improve adoption decisions.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Savings claims not matched to shop-floor data
Credit constraints and behaviour underexplored
Decision-makers lack independent evidence
outputs: Measured adoption barriers and cost drivers
A practical scale-up and finance case

public.label: 05 / INVESTMENT CLIMATE REFORM
public.title: Reducing the cost of doing business through better rules.
public.desc: Complex licensing, unclear institutional mandates and uneven administrative practice can suppress private investment even when demand exists. Reform needs evidence, coordination and delivery oversight.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Duplicated procedures and unclear requirements
Private-sector feedback poorly structured
Reforms not linked to measurable implementation
public.outputTitle: A reform programme that can be delivered.

private.label: 05 / PRIVATE INVESTMENT & COMPLIANCE
private.title: Locating the hidden costs in an expansion decision.
private.desc: Business growth can be blocked by an accumulation of small frictions: permits, land access, logistics, time costs, financing and uncertain administrative practice.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.problemTitle: A growth plan with invisible regulatory costs.
problems: Permit timelines absent from the business plan
Site and logistics constraints underpriced
Investor milestones and approvals misaligned
